subject: general
question: A class consisting of 30 students took a competitive exam. 18 of these students got an average of 90 marks and the remaining students of this class got an average of 80 marks. What is the average score of the class as a whole?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of number of students = 18 : 12 = 3 : 2 and assumed base average = 80.

Deviation for the first group = 90 − 80 = 10.

Net deviation distributed over total = (3 × 10) ÷ (3 + 2) = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

Combined Average = Base average + Net deviation = 80 + 6 = 86 marks.

**∴ The correct answer is 86 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of students = 30

Number of students with an average of 90 marks = 18

Number of remaining students = 30 − 18 = 12

Average marks of the remaining 12 students = 80

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 Ratio = 3
 Ratio = 2
 
 
 
 
 18 Students
 Avg: 90
 
 12 Students
 Avg: 80
 
 

 Total 30 Students → Avg = 86

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks of the first 18 students = 18 × 90 = 1620

⇒ Total marks of the remaining 12 students = 12 × 80 = 960

⇒ Total sum of marks of all 30 students = 1620 + 960 = 2580

⇒ Average score of the class = 2580 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score of the class = 86 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 86 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is used to find the average of two or more groups with different numbers of items. The formula is Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method

To calculate the average quickly, assume a base average and calculate the net deviation. Formula: New Average = Base + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Total Count).

Rule of Alligation

This method visually connects the averages of two groups to the combined average. The ratio of the quantities is inversely proportional to the differences in their averages.
